metadata.title: On the Cohen-Macaulay property for quadratic tangent cones

extraction_notes.note: The direct implication of Theorem 1.8 is a prose proof spread over Section 3 and its (sub)subsections; split into one proof node per heading, each with a proves edge to TP7. With many parts, the continuation edges form a tree (case parts -> case setup -> Section 3 reduction -> PP3) rather than all pointing at the first part.
The Case (A) and Case (B) setups are tiny proof parts (an assumption, plus for Case (B) the elimination of lambda''); emitted only because the subsection headings split the proof.
Numbered equation (2) is the Eisenbud-Green-Harris growth bound, named in the text; retyped from equation to an external theorem.
remark or claim: self-contained observations, argued in place, from the screening setup before Theorem 2.4; kept as remarks since no separate statement is proved.
The corollary has no proof; it is read off the case analysis in the proof of Theorem 2.4 (non-Koszul only for e(H) in 9,10,11), so it is marked semi_formal.

Table 1 (h-vectors of quadratic 5-generated semigroups with examples) is computational data and has no node. The Roos-Sturmfels comparison paragraph and the introduction's restatements of the main results also have none.
The h-polynomial and h-vector are defined twice (Introduction and Section 2); only the Introduction copy is a node.

$$

$$

There are though, up to a permutation of the variables, a couple of candidates for J which do not admit a quadratic Gr\"obner basis with respect to any term order. We present these exceptions in Remark . item If h_2=4= binom32+ binom11, then h_3 leq 1 and h_4=0. We scanned the possible candidates for J and we eliminated those ideals where the resolution of K over barR (computed with Singular ) is becoming nonlinear after at most 5 steps. All the other candidates had a quadratic Gr\"obner bases with respect to revlex (usually induced by x_2>x_3>x_4>x_5) and even a Gr\"obner flag. All the non-Koszul ideals were among those with h_3=0, hence with e(H)=9. item If h_2=5= binom32+ binom21, then by we get h_3leq 2 and h_4=0. It is well known and easy to see that if barR is Koszul, then its Poincar\'e series equals 1/H(-t). It is routine to check that if h_3=0 then 1/H(-t)= 1+4t+cdots -29x^6+cdots, and if h_3=1 then 1/H(-t)= 1+4t+cdots -174 x^8+cdots. Therefore, in either case R is not Koszul. However, if h_3=2 then e(H)= 12=2^4-2^2 and we may apply Theorem to conclude that H is G-quadratic. item If h_2=6, then I_H^* is a complete intersection, hence H is G-quadratic. This finishes the proof of the theorem.

		We consider the possible even values of $a_1$. 
		\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=0.5cm, label*=\arabic*.]
		 \item If \underline{$a_1=6$} we obtain the other generators
			\begin{eqnarray*}
				a_2 &=& 4u+2u''+w''u',\\
				a_3 &=& 3u', \\
				a_4 &=&2u+4u''+2w''u', \\
				a_5 &=& 6u+6u''+ (3w''+3)u'-6.
			\end{eqnarray*}
			Note that $a_5 = (u+u''-1) a_1+ (w''+1) a_3\in \langle a_1, a_3 \rangle$, which is false.
		 \item If \underline{$a_1=8$ or $12$}, then $a_2,a_3, a_4$ are even, hence $a_5$ is even as well, a contradiction.
		 \item If \underline{$a_1=10$}, then it easy to see that $a_2,a_3, a_4, a_5$ are divisible by $5$, which is false.

		\end{enumerate}

							a_5 &=& 4u+6u''+7u'-8,  \nonumber
					 \end{eqnarray}
					which turn out to be of the desired form.
			\end{enumerate}
	\end{enumerate}
